record.context_brief: Free-product cancellation up to elementary equivalence
record.original_question: Let I and J be finite sets, and let {N_i}_{i∈I} and {M_j}_{j∈J} be families of separable II_1 factors such that the free products *_{i∈I} N_i^U and *_{j∈J} M_j^U are isomorphic. Must |I|=|J|, and after permuting indices, must the corresponding factors be elementarily equivalent?

evidence.quote: Problem 50. Suppose I, J are finite sets, and {Ni}i∈I , {Mj}j∈J are separable II1 factors such that ∗i∈INU i ∼= ∗j∈JMU j , then is I ∼= J and the factors are mutually elementarily equivalent up to permutation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I$ and $J$ be finite nonempty index sets. For each $i \in I$ let $N_i$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, and for each $j \in J$ let $M_j$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. Fix a free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and for a tracial von Neumann algebra $P$ let $P^{\mathcal{U}}$ denote the tracial ultrapower of $P$ along $\mathcal{U}$. Consider the (von Neumann algebraic) free products with respect to the canonical traces:
$$\Asterisk_{i \in I} N_i^{\mathcal{U}} \quad \text{and} \quad \Asterisk_{j \in J} M_j^{\mathcal{U}}.$$
Suppose that these two free products are isomorphic as von Neumann algebras. Must it then follow that $|I| = |J|$, and that there exists a bijection $\sigma : I \to J$ such that for every $i \in I$ the $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors $N_i$ and $M_{\sigma(i)}$ are elementarily equivalent in the language of tracial von Neumann algebras (equivalently, $N_i^{\mathcal{U}} \cong M_{\sigma(i)}^{\mathcal{U}}$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of fifty open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors. While related results show the existence of non-elementarily equivalent II_1 factors and free-product rigidity in various contexts, no source found resolves this specific cancellation/elementary-equivalence statement for free products of ultrapowers. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Two non-elementarily equivalent II_1 factors without property Gamma
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of separable II_1 factors that are not elementarily equivalent, using amalgamated free products.
status_evidence.claim: Related work distinguishes II_1 factors via elementary equivalence but does not resolve the free-product cancellation problem.

status_evidence.title: An exotic II_1 factor without property Gamma
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit examples of non-elementarily equivalent II_1 factors.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances on elementary equivalence of II_1 factors do not address this specific free-product cancellation question.
